extracted.intended_audience: CVPR 2022 reviewers, area chairs, and reviewers-in-training (computer vision conference peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policies for writing reviews and making accept/reject recommendations for CVPR 2022 submissions, including what to include/avoid in reviews and new conference policies. Targets reviewers and area chairs evaluating computer-vision conference papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum reviewer coverage and thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 3 reviewers each provides one thorough expert review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper submissions are assigned to ACs; reviewers should each provide a thorough, expert review to support AC recommendations and program chair decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and transparency of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: We want it to be a fair and transparent process for every paper; the authors are explicitly informed on WHY their paper is accepted/rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may appeal only if they identified potential biases in the process; appealing simply the specific decision is not valid. Strive for the most informed decision given paper, reviews, rebuttals, and discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent, objective, critical, and comprehensive review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an independent, objective, critical, and comprehensive review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain clearly the basis of your review and recommendation; be willing to discuss with AC and reviewer buddies to reach consensus but it's OK to disagree after discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess knowledge advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Key: What is the knowledge advancement in the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on whether the paper presents sufficient, well-grounded knowledge advancement rather than only on superficial factors (e.g., raw novelty or beating SOTA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make recommendations with solid justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your final recommendations with solid justifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the rebuttal and discussions; explicitly state whether and why these change your position to facilitate AC decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be constructive and suggest improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Be constructive to the authors: it is necessary to be critical, but avoid offending the authors; instead, suggest how they could make the paper better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable suggestions for improvement rather than only negative judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism in interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be friendly to your buddy reviewers and ACs; focus discussions on the technical side and do not take it personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree to disagree; avoid personal attacks or unprofessional language; maintain collegial tone in discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Be on time, responsible, and responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any delay will impose additional workload on colleagues; timely reviews support a fair process and allow rebuttal/discussion phases to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ACs for procedural or ethical help
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need any help in the process, your ACs are there to help you; suspicious ethical/mischief concerns should be raised to ACs and PCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid policing the paper directly on such issues; inform ACs/PCs about ethics concerns instead of acting as enforcers yourself. ACs also track reviewer reputation and nominate outstanding reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criteria: knowledge advancement and audience interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any paper that, in accordance with CVPR community standards, presents sufficient knowledge advancement that is well grounded; is of sufficient interest to some CVPR audiences who could benefit from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVPR is inclusive; rejection solely for out-of-scope is rare. Evaluate both the substantive advancement and the paper's interest to parts of the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise summary in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a concise summary of the paper: What problem is addressed? Is it a new problem? If not, why does it still matter? What is the key to the solution? What is the main contribution? Do the experiments sufficiently support the claims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short, accurate summary helps authors and ACs immediately understand the reviewer's view of the paper's contributions and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear statement of strengths and weaknesses: What are the key contributions and why do they matter? What aspects of the paper most need improvement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize main strengths and weaknesses; indicate which weaknesses are fatal and which are fixable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive check for fundamental flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a comprehensive check of potential fundamental flaws in the paper: Are the assumptions and theories (mathematically) sound? Are the experiments scientifically sound and valid? Is the problem addressed trivial? Did the paper miss important prior work? Has it been done before? If yes, where?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish minor issues from fundamental problems that invalidate the main claims; provide evidence and references when claiming missing prior work or flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arrogance, ignorance, and inaccuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not display arrogance, ignorance, or inaccuracy in reviews (examples include asserting 'the only way is my way' or factual mistakes about the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe behavior: do not provide an opinion on things you do not know about; check facts before asserting them; be humble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pure opinions; ground statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid making pure opinions without grounding (e.g., 'This is not good enough for CVPR 2022' without justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe behavior: ground your statements with a 'because ...' explaining the evidence or reasoning behind subjective judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the novelty fallacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept or reject a paper solely based on perceived novelty (either 'not novel' or 'novel means good').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many important things are not that novel and many novel things are not important. Focus on whether the paper presents well-grounded knowledge advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blank assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid making ungrounded statements (e.g., 'This has been done before' without citations, or generalizations like 'Intrinsic images are no longer important').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence to support assertions; confine discussion to technical content rather than attacking authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid policy entrepreneurism
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not impose your own policies (e.g., 'You must publish your dataset', 'You must beat SOTA', 'You must have a theorem').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are not official review policies. Follow common principles in scientific review and focus on knowledge advancement rather than personal checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid intellectual laziness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overemphasize single factors (e.g., 'Does not beat SOTA so it must be rejected' or 'Beat SOTA so it must be accepted').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether identified errors actually invalidate the main knowledge advancement. Provide comprehensive assessment rather than mechanically weighting one metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Data contributions must include dataset URL when claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that claim data releases as one of their key contributions need to provide a URL for the data by the camera-ready deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check if the authors flagged this in the author submission form (visible in CMT). Explicitly comment in the review form if a paper claimed data contribution but did not flag it, which alerts the meta-reviewer. This discourages 'dataset papers' that do not actually provide data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Attribution of data assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are advised that they need to cite data assets used (e.g., datasets or code) much like papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat used data assets just like previous work in the form of papers; expect proper citation and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Personal data / human subjects require IRB/ethics description
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is using personal data or data from human subjects, the authors must have an ethics clearance from an IRB and provide a statement in the paper or supplementary material that the IRB approval has already been obtained. If no IRB exists, authors must clearly describe adherence to ethical principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IRB approval is present, nothing to do. If such a paper does NOT have IRB approval but shows ethical principles were followed, this is acceptable. If there is no description or there are glaring ethical violations, inform the ACs and the PCs. CVPR does not (yet) have an ethics review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Discussion of potential negative societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include a discussion on potential negative societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not formally required and you cannot reject a paper solely for not providing such a discussion. Weigh the inclusion of a meaningful discussion positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Discussion of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to explicitly and honestly discuss limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT penalize papers for honestly discussing limitations; instead, weigh the inclusion of an honest limitations discussion positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Social media ban during review period
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should NOT use social media to promote their paper submissions to CVPR during the review period (social media silence period defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers find a paper suspicious of violating the policy, report to the corresponding Area Chairs and Program Chairs, who will investigate. Continue to review the paper as if there is no violation. If ACs and PCs conclude a violation occurred, the paper could be desk rejected. Refer to FAQ for policy related to arXiv and project pages.
